footnotes.text: Waves of compression and rarefaction that are capable of producing sound. Speed of sound in the air at 20° C at sea level is 344 m/s (1120 ft).
Sound travels faster in liquids and solids than in the air.
When sound energy passes from air to liquid medium, most of its energy is reflected back because of the impedance offered by the liquid.
A person under water cannot hear any sound made in the air because 99.9% of the sound energy is reflected away from the surface of water because of the impedance offered by water.
